review_basis: registered O4-PHY-1 printed p.93-94 oxidation/reduction scope
semantic distinctness, exam relevance and no-filler policy

decisions.rationale: Electron transfer is the central substantive redox proposition and opens the previously uncovered chemical-change target.
Extending oxidation/reduction from oxygen or hydrogen transfer to electron transfer is a useful conceptual boundary rather than a wording duplicate of C006.
The simultaneity of oxidation and reduction is an independently testable redox principle.
Oxidation-number increase/decrease is a distinct explanatory representation of redox beyond direct electron-transfer language.
The item asks which reagent names the curriculum document lists rather than testing what an oxidizing or reducing agent does; source-catalog recall is insufficient incremental Otsu4 practice value.
Merely recalling that ionization tendency is mentioned beside redox does not test the underlying chemical relationship.
Merely recalling that the Daniell cell is mentioned beside redox is curriculum-association recall rather than a substantive cell or redox proposition.

collision_review.note: The canonical 205 contain no answer-defining chemical-change target collision. C010-C012 are rejected for insufficient educational value, leaving four substantive redox concepts without quota backfill.

source_review_scope: This gate checks source registration, locator reproducibility and answer-binding completeness; final canonical source verification remains separate after Permanent ID integration.
